description:
FILED s516 (Fable, 2026-10-12) from the s515c review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p516c/ovr.pl vs ovr2.pl; outputs beside them).  PRE-EXISTING on main edc64d62 and on both the s515a (has #3184) and s515c trees.

The two spellings of the same import diverge at the PARSE:
  use File::Glob qw(:bsd_glob);  my @l = glob("$d/a b.txt");   -> emission (pl-glob ...) + (p-use "File::Glob" :import-args (vector ":bsd_glob"))  -> 1 file = perl, in list AND scalar AND <> AND iterator shapes
  use File::Glob ':bsd_glob';    my @l = glob("$d/a b.txt");   -> emission (p-glob ...)  + (p-use "File::Glob" :import-args ":bsd_glob")           -> 2 (word-split), perl 1; two words "$d/c.txt $d/e.txt" -> 2, perl 1
So whatever feeds the builtin-override recorder (the `glob` entry of the :bsd_glob tag in the File::Glob facts overlay) reads a qw() list and not a single quoted string -- the import-list reader #3184 widened for TAG names from arrays may be the place (check how a `use M "name"` bare-quote import reaches it: s514f #3143 says the bare-quote import asks the module's package first).  The detector DOES announce the 2 sites under PCL_DETECT=announce (the shim installs main::glob at run time either way), so this is a detector-visible silent wrong: the value is wrong AND the announcement is right.

Same mechanism family as #3206 (whose cause the same probe located: under the qw spelling the parse emits pl-glob -- it DID consult the override -- yet the detector table registers the site as ("main" "glob" N "builtin"); the TABLE is wrong, not the parse).  Both go into the next correctness brief, which also flips the detector default back to announce (USER ruling s516).  Guard: a Pl/t row per spelling (list + scalar context, a real directory with a space-named file), perl-compared; the quoted-string rows must fail on main.

=== DONE (s516a) ===
Pl::Parser::bare_quote_import_names is THE reading of an unparenthesised quoted import list (a string is an import name when the MODULE knows it: a declared sub, an @EXPORT/@EXPORT_OK name, or a :tag in its import sets); the prototype merge (#733) and Parser2::_use_imported_names (the override recorder) both call it, and _use_imported_names expands tags through Parser::_expand_import_tags (its second copy of the tag expansion is gone).  use File::Glob ':bsd_glob' is now the same import as qw(:bsd_glob): ovr2.pl = perl (1 / 1).  Guard Pl/t/glob-override-01.t rows 1-3 (single-quoted, double-quoted, parenthesised; fail on main).  Commit f507e002 (s516a).
subject: use File::Glob ':bsd_glob' (a single QUOTED STRING, not qw) does not install the glob override: the call stays the builtin p-glob, csh word-splitting stays (perl 1 file, PCL 2) -- the builtin-override recorder reads a qw() import list only
